sections.content: How many people are "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)"?

16,335 people

were counted on the census as "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.

People who do this type of work may perform a variety of tasks in relation to the breeding and rearing of animals and fish, catch fish at sea and from inland waterways, assist in the picking and lifting of crops, plant and maintain hedges, oversee the incubation and hatching of eggs and perform other fishing and elementary agricultural tasks not elsewhere classified.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)", 14% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)" was 65 years or older.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)" included:

  • shelf fillers
  • elementary administration occupations (other)
  • pharmacy and optical dispensing assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)" there were more men than women (69.7% compared with 30.3%).

This means "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary trades and related occupations".

Men made up 69.7% and women made up 30.3% of "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)" included:

  • print finishing and binding workers
  • health and safety managers and officers
  • upholsterers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)", 10% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (71.2% compared with 28.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (80.2%) than self-employed (19.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
